newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto offers self for graft probe under new law.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto offers self for graft probe under new law.

text.p: Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto proposed a new anti-corruption measure to Pakistan's parliament on Sunday, seeking all-party support and promising that she herself would be the first to submit to scrutiny.

The bill would permit public servants from president to provincial legislators, senior officials, judges and military officers to be summoned before a parliamentary committee in which opposition and government have equal weight.

If the committee finds a case to answer, corruption charges would be tried by two high court judges who could impose prison sentences up to seven years, levy fines, confiscate ill-gotten property, and disqualify those convicted from office.
"I offer myself to be the first person to face accountability," Bhutto told parliament.
She said she wanted all accusation raised by the opposition against herself and her businessman husband Asif Ali Zardari fully investigated so that others could not complain of discrimination.
The proposal requires a constitutional ammendment, meaning Bhutto does not have the votes in parliament to pass it without opposition support.

It would apply to holders of public office since July 5, 1977, the day General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq overthrew Benazir Bhutto's father, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who was later executed. Zia ruled Pakistan for 11 years and until his death in a still unexplained plane crash.
If the parliamentary committee were deadlocked on whether to press a corruption charge, it would be referred to the National Assembly or, in the case of lawmakers, to the house concerned.
